title: Whatever Whatever
intro: The title's indifference is surrounded by care. A casual call becomes an earnest plea to an old friend to stay alive; a scene of exhausting social behaviour then produces the wish to disappear. 'Whatever' works as a boundary around other people's entanglements, not a statement that nobody matters. Crucially, the song returns to the friend after that refrain. Its final commitment is selective and intimate: he cannot take responsibility for every situation, but this person's continued existence matters to him.
reading: Selective care rather than universal indifference; the final return to the friend determines the emotional landing.

revisions.16-poison: The opening promises to sort out every problem and remain immune to poison. Addressed through a call or message, that confidence can also do reassuring work for somebody else. It need not be a transparent report of an invulnerable inner state. The later stifling boredom and desire to disappear expose the limits of the claim. The voice can offer steadiness to a friend while struggling to remain comfortable in the wider scene.
revisions.editorial-16-live-well: He asks the friend to keep living for the friend's own sake. That matters beside a record full of money, usefulness and other people's demands: continued existence does not have to be justified by producing something for an audience. The everyday blessing of eating and drinking prepares this modest standard. When these lines return at the end, after repeated 'whatever', they establish what his withdrawal is meant to leave room for.
revisions.16-inhale: The speaker says 'I guess', then declines to hear details. Ear studs and gold teeth become grounds for a judgement he does not verify. Keeping that wording visible prevents the annotation from endorsing the stereotype as fact. It also reveals how estranged he already feels: the people are legible to him as a type before they are individuals he wants to understand. His longing to be invisible grows out of this failed contact.
revisions.16-whatever: The earlier phrase 'pretending not to care' gives this refrain its limit. He is trying to stop other people's relationships and behaviour from becoming his responsibility. The song then returns to asking an old friend to live well, so indifference does not get the last word. This is a distinction between care he chooses and involvement he cannot bear, rather than a simple progression from compassion to not caring about anyone.
